2786391.title: Gwangalli M Drone Light Show
2786391.overview: Every Saturday night, 1,100 drones fly a choreographed show over the water at Gwangalli Beach, with the illuminated Gwangan Bridge behind them. It has run since 2022 — the M stands for Marvelous — and it is free, with no ticket and no seating: you watch from anywhere along the beach. Each show lasts about 12 minutes and there are two a night, at 20:00 and 22:00 from March to September, an hour earlier in winter. For New Year's countdown, Seollal and Chuseok the fleet scales up to as many as 3,000 drones. Shows are cancelled in bad weather, so check before making the trip.
2786391.hours: Saturdays · Mar–Sep 20:00 and 22:00 · Oct–Feb 19:00 and 21:00 · about 12 minutes

3113265.title: APAP Art Tour (Anyang Public Art Project)
3113265.overview: Since 2005 Anyang has been installing permanent public artworks along its forests, streams, roadsides and ordinary parks, with the aim of turning the whole city into a museum without a roof. This guided walking tour covers work from the first seven editions of the project, across Anyang Art Park and the Pyeongchon district, led by a docent who explains the sculpture, architecture, design and performance pieces and how they relate to the city's history. Tours run twice daily, Tuesday to Sunday, and last 60–90 minutes. Anyang is about 40 minutes south of Seoul.
3113265.place: Anyang Pavilion (Anyang Art Park) and Pyeongchon Central Park
3113265.fee: Adults 3,000 won · Under 19s 1,000 won (special tours priced separately)

293030.title: Gombaengi Teotta: Anseong Namsadang Baudeogi Troupe Resident Performance
293030.overview: Namsadang were travelling troupes of male entertainers who toured Korean market towns from the Joseon period, and Anseong was their home base — Baudeogi, the only woman ever to lead one, is a local legend. The city's municipal troupe has performed here since 2003, and the 2026 programme restages the six traditional namsadang acts. Expect taepyeongso and kkwaenggwari-driven percussion, eoreum — tightrope walking three metres up, with the walker trading jokes with a partner below — plate spinning on sticks, and acrobatic tumbling. Every Saturday and Sunday at 14:00, about 90 minutes.
293030.fee: Adults 12,000 won · Youth 6,000 won · Children 3,000 won (50% off for Anseong residents and seniors)

3497454.title: Traditional Culture Programme at the Uijeongbu Site
3497454.overview: The Uijeongbu was the highest council of the Joseon government, and its excavated site now forms a public historical plaza on Sejong-daero, a few minutes from Gwanghwamun. The programme staged here recreates yeolmu — the military review drills of the Samgunbu troops once garrisoned along this street of six ministries — alongside a chance to try seunggyeongdo, a Joseon board game about climbing the official ranks, and hands-on traditional martial arts. Free, and easy to fold into a day at the palaces, since it runs late morning to mid-afternoon.

4089090.title: Earthenware: The Common Pots That Held Us
4089090.overview: A special exhibition at the Gwangju National Museum on Korean earthenware — the unglazed and coarsely glazed pots used for storing, fermenting and carrying, as opposed to the celadon and porcelain that usually represent Korean ceramics abroad. Around 300 objects are shown, including a ribbed bottle and large storage jars excavated from the Cheonghaejin garrison site on Jangdo Island, Wando. Free.
4089090.place: Special Exhibition Hall, Gwangju National Museum

4087092.title: GHOST Festival 2026 (Gyeonggi Hallyu OST)
4087092.overview: A three-day music festival built entirely around soundtracks — the songs from K-dramas, Korean films and animation — performed alongside K-pop artists. Each day takes a different theme: romance, science fiction, fantasy, running from ballads through band sets to full orchestra, with large-scale media art staging. There are also K-content activities, food and camping on site. The setting is unusual: Imjingak Peace Nuri Park sits directly against the DMZ in Paju, about an hour from Seoul.
4087092.fee: 1-day 120,000 won · 2-day 180,000 won · 3-day 240,000 won (early bird 1-day 96,000 won) · 50% off secondary students · Free for preschoolers and over-65s

1725993.title: Goyang Autumn Flower Festival
1725993.overview: An autumn flower show at Ilsan Lake Park in Goyang, one of the largest artificial lake parks in Asia and about 40 minutes northwest of central Seoul. The planting is arranged as much for sitting among as for looking at — the point is an afternoon in the park rather than a horticultural exhibition. Free. Not to be confused with the much larger International Horticulture Goyang Korea, which runs in spring at the same venue.

3522298.title: Drone Soccer World Cup Jeonju 2025
3522298.overview: The first Drone Soccer World Cup, held in the plaza outside Jeonju World Cup Stadium over four days in September 2025, marking ten years since the sport was invented — in Jeonju. Drone soccer is played with caged drones that score by flying through a hoop, and national teams came from around the world to compete. Alongside the tournament ran a crashing competition, a super-pilot selection event, an international drone industry symposium, performances, and drone try-out sessions for visitors. Free.
3522298.sponsor: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport · Jeonbuk State · Jeonju City · FIDA

2737313.title: Seomjin River International Experimental Art Festival 2025 (SIEAF)
2737313.overview: An experimental and performance art festival held along the Seomjingang, the river running through Gokseong in the south of the country. The 2025 theme was 'Seomjingang Byeolgok' — byeolgok being a form of folk song that carried private stories of ordinary lives — reworked so that the lives and legends along the river are told in the language of contemporary art. Around 100 artists from Korea and abroad took part, with work staged outdoors at the Amnok riverside recreation area. Free; times varied by programme.

3576410.title: Gwangbok-ro Winter Light Tree Festival
3576410.overview: Busan's main winter illumination, running along Gwangbok-ro in the old town from a countdown switch-on in early December through to late February. During the festival there is busking by Busan musicians, and public switch-on events where visitors light the trees themselves. Free, and directly connected to the Day 1 route in our Busan guide — Gwangbok-ro runs alongside BIFF Square and Gukje Market, so the illuminations are a natural way to end an afternoon in the old town.

4054203.title: Yi Sun-sin Festival
4054203.overview: Admiral Yi Sun-sin — the naval commander who defeated a far larger Japanese fleet at Myeongnyang in 1597, and the most revered figure in Korean military history — was born in what is now Jung-gu, Seoul, and the district holds a birthday festival at the site. It is staged as a party rather than a commemoration: a giant birthday cake carrying 481 messages, a naval honour guard parade, an 'Iron Man Yi Sun-sin' contest for residents, and stage performances. A food zone brings together 20 of the district's restaurants, a flea market sells Yi Sun-sin merchandise, and the activity area runs from paper-hat making and calligraphy to VR horseback riding, turtle-ship puzzles and a Roblox birthday party.
4054203.place: Around Yi Sun-sin's birthplace, near Myeongbo Art Hall

3509748.title: EX Horror Season 6: Silla X Zombie
3509748.overview: A walk-through horror attraction staged after dark in the Hwarang Forest at Gyeongju Expo Park, along a 2 km woodland trail dressed with set pieces and live performers. It draws more than 15,000 visitors a year. The 2026 season sets zombies loose in Silla-era Gyeongju. Open to all ages, though the operator advises against it for anyone elderly or with a medical condition, and preschool children must be accompanied by an adult. Later and slightly cheaper on weekdays.
3509748.fee: Mon–Thu 10,000 won · Fri–Sun and holidays 12,000 won (discount for online booking)

3537267.title: Baengnyeon Night Market: Return of the Catfish
3537267.overview: Baengnyeon Market is a traditional market in northern Seoul by day and a night market twice a year, and it was named the country's best culture-and-tourism market in 2025. Under a giant mirror ball at the centre, bingo games and performances run while each section of the market has its own DJ set, games and events. Visitors choose the songs played through the alleys, and receipts from market stalls convert into tokens for events and cocktails. Rather than a stage that everyone faces, the design keeps you moving through the market itself. Free entry; food and drink are paid for individually.
3537267.fee: Free entry (food and drink charged separately)
3537267.sponsor: Ministry of SMEs and Startups · Seoul Metropolitan Government · Gangbuk-gu

4100347.title: Pohang Ten Tastes Night Food Festival
4100347.overview: Pohang has an official list of ten local dishes, and this two-day night market puts them on the street under festoon lighting in the Munduk district. The ten are mori guksu (a spicy fish noodle stew), Pohang mulhoe (raw fish in cold broth), blue-fish hoe, gwamegi (half-dried herring, a Pohang speciality eaten in winter), snow crab, ox-head soup, bibimbap with Pohang spinach and mountain greens, grilled clams at Yeongildae, monkfish soup and haesintang. Alongside the food stalls there are DJ sets, a singing contest, a small-trader flea market and a children's fire-engine zone. Free, and run with reusable tableware.
